description:
Start native profiling on a booted device. iOS: Instruments via xctrace (CPU, hangs, memory leaks). Android: Perfetto (CPU, jank, RSS-growth weak signal).
After starting, let the user interact with the app, then call native-profiler-stop.
Use when you want to capture native CPU, hang, and memory data for a running app.
Returns { status, pid, traceFile } confirming the recording has started. On Android, a warning names the apps with native network capture on (started by native-network-logs): their timings in the profile can differ.
Fails if no app is running on the device, or the profiler cannot attach to the process.

app_process.description: iOS: the CFBundleExecutable or display name of the app to profile. Android: the app's package name. If omitted, auto-detects the foreground app; set it only if auto-detection picks the wrong app.

device_id.description: Target device id from `list-devices` (iOS UDID or Android serial).

malloc_stack_logging.description: iOS only. When true, cold-launches the app under the profiler with Malloc Stack Logging enabled so memory leaks carry an allocation backtrace (responsible frame + library). Without it, leaks carry no backtrace (Instruments reports '<Call stack limit reached>'). Trade-offs: this RESTARTS the app (current state is lost), adds memory/CPU overhead, and makes the app noticeably slow to launch, so leave it off for pure CPU/hang profiling. Rejected up front under the all-processes capture (used where Xcode's `--device` recording is broken, or forced with ARGENT_IOS_CAPTURE=all-processes), which cannot cold-launch and records no leaks.

template_path.description: iOS only. Path to an Instruments .tracetemplate file (defaults to the bundled Argent template).

name: native-profiler-start
